market_observations:
The Houston market for fractional/virtual executive assistant services is THIN on the agency side and DIFFUSE on the solo side, creating a genuine first-mover window for a professionally branded Houston-based fractional EA firm targeting senior executives.

1. LOCAL AGENCY LANDSCAPE IS SPARSE: Only two verifiable Houston-native EA/VA agencies with real web presence emerged: Robert Lee and Associates (founded 2021, Wix site, no pricing, 2 employees, good positioning) and Sky Virtual Solutions (Galleria, basic Ueni builder site, 20-year experience claim, banking/finance focus). EntreAdmin is Houston-based but serves trades/SMBs at $1,500-$3,000/mo, not senior corporate executives. JDK Virtuals exists but is primarily a medical VA firm with a Philippines delivery model. No Houston agency explicitly serves the energy executive, healthcare C-suite, or legal partner tier with Houston-specific positioning.

2. NATIONAL COMPETITORS FILL THE VACUUM WITH SEO PAGES: ExecViva (pricing: $3,999/mo, polished Houston landing page), VirtualEZ (Canadian-led), Virtual Synergy Inc. ($9/hr, WY-based), and Vera Outsourcing (SF-based, <200 visits/month) all target Houston via SEO without local presence. This is an SEO gap — a genuinely Houston-based firm with deep local industry knowledge could outrank national SEO pages over time.

3. SOLOS ARE THE MAIN LOCAL 'FRACTIONAL' MARKET: The fractional/virtual EA space is currently dominated by LinkedIn-visible solo operators — Mickey B. (BusbyLife, 22 years), Halee Harris (Handled by Halee, 2025 launch), Anna Baker (fractional partner, 2025 launch), Lara Kuhleman-Valdez (oil & gas EA background, currently employed). Solos have capacity limits and no backup coverage — the exact gap an agency model addresses.

4. GROUP C STAFFING FIRMS ARE STRONG BUT IN A DIFFERENT LANE: Murray Resources ($15M revenue, 21K visits/mo), Burnett Specialists ($12M revenue, 50K visits/mo), Frontline Source Group (5-year warranty, 5.0 Trustpilot), and Robert Half (global) dominate in-person EA placement. They serve the buyer who wants to hire a W-2 employee — not the buyer who wants on-demand fractional or virtual support. These are not direct competitors for the fractional/virtual model but they do compete for the same executive buyer's attention and budget intent.

5. WEBSITE QUALITY IS GENERALLY LOW IN LOCAL VA SEGMENT: Most local Houston VA/EA sites score 2-3/5 — basic builders (Wix, Ueni), no pricing transparency, minimal SEO content, no industry specialization pages. The bar to be the 'most professional Houston-based fractional EA website' is very low. Robert Half and Frontline Source Group set the ceiling but serve a different model.

6. PRICING ANCHORS: ExecViva publishes $3,999/mo for full-time EA. EntreAdmin publishes $1,500-$3,000/mo for SMB-tier ops support. Virtual Synergy ($9/hr offshore) anchors the bottom. Robert Half places in-person EAs at $60-80K/yr ($5,000-$6,667/mo all-in cost to employer). This means fractional EA pricing of $2,000-$4,500/mo for part-time or fractional support is well within market norms and compares favorably to both offshore ($9/hr) and in-person hiring ($5-7K/mo with benefits).

7. BIGGEST GAP IDENTIFIED: No competitor explicitly positions as a Houston-based fractional/virtual EA serving the energy industry, Texas Medical Center/healthcare C-suite, legal partners, or PE/family office principals with industry-specific language and Houston credibility. This is the most defensible position in the market.
